sources.note: Casts benchmark contamination auditing as sparse-mixture detection, proves that detectability is governed by the single quantity alpha*rho*sqrt(m), and shows empirically that the resulting power predictions transport while the sample-size budgets derived from them do not.
sources.title: When Is Benchmark Contamination Detectable? Information Limits and Power-Calibrated Audits

sources.note: Reverse-engineers the arithmetic circuit down to individual neurons and finds it is neither a learned algorithm nor memorization, but an unordered collection of sparse heuristic neurons that each fire on a numerical input pattern and vote for corresponding answers.
sources.title: Arithmetic Without Algorithms: Language Models Solve Math With a Bag of Heuristics

sources.note: Trains sparse autoencoders on language model activations to recover an overcomplete dictionary of sparsely activating directions, and shows those directions are more interpretable and more precisely causal than neurons, PCA or ICA.
sources.title: Sparse Autoencoders Find Highly Interpretable Features in Language Models

result.definition: A small open model with a fully documented training corpus, and across 3 sources the checkpoint used where the training data must be known. That property is load-bearing in two of them: it is the only model for which a contamination study can verify that a base checkpoint is uncontaminated, and it is where sparse-autoencoder feature quality is measured against interpretability baselines layer by layer. It is also a subject in arithmetic circuit analysis. Its small size means results on it bound what is possible rather than what happens at scale, which the sources state.
